2_Introduction: The champion device showed a PCE of 23.2049%, with JSC of 26.442 mA/cm², FF of 76.0187%, and VOC of 1.1544 V. The Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. Afterwards, the perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then at 5500 rpm for 30 s. The addition of 150 µL antisolvent at last 15 s proved instrumental in achieving uniform film thickness and grain distribution. Then the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min to form the perovskite layer.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-concentration Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3 precursor, with its A-site cation alloying optimizing the tolerance factor for enhanced phase stability and suppressed ion migration, was deposited via a two-step spin-coating process where an initial 1000 rpm spread promoted uniform wetting before a rapid 5500 rpm acceleration, coupled with the precise introduction of 150 µL antisolvent at the final 15-second mark, triggered a controlled, rapid supersaturation that seeded a high density of nucleation sites while the immediate solvent expulsion suppressed the re-dissolution of nuclei, thereby directing the crystallization toward a uniform morphological foundation with reduced pinhole formation. Subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 minutes then facilitated the coalescence and lateral growth of these nuclei into a dense, large-grain polycrystalline film, effectively healing point defects and minimizing non-radiative recombination pathways at grain boundaries through Ostwald ripening, which collectively enhanced charge carrier lifetimes and transport. This meticulously engineered crystallization trajectory, devoid of secondary phases and with optimized grain boundary network, directly translated into superior photovoltaic parameters, yielding a champion device with a VOC of 1.1544 V, a JSC of 26.442 mA/cm², an FF of 76.0187%, and a resulting PCE of 23.2049%.
